## Core Problem

How can geometric collision awareness be internalized into VLA weights during training — rather than applied as inference-time guidance or post-hoc correction — so that the model generates inherently safe actions in a single forward pass with zero additional inference cost?

## Opportunity / Why Now

OmniGuide (arXiv 2603.10052, Mar 2026) demonstrates that differentiable SDF gradients can dramatically improve VLA collision avoidance (7.0% → 93.5% CAR on RoboCasa) via inference-time guidance fields. However, OmniGuide operates exclusively at inference time: it requires iterative gradient computation through differentiable kinematics at each denoising step, adding ~2x latency (30Hz → 15Hz), inherits potential field local minima in dense clutter, and only works with diffusion/flow-matching VLAs. The VLA safety survey (arXiv 2604.23775, Apr 2026) identifies a safety–performance tension: CBF-based corrections can push VLA trajectories out-of-distribution, as AEGIS/VLSA (arXiv 2512.11891) explicitly acknowledges — 'the AEGIS may adjust the trajectory to unfamiliar regions...statistically rare or absent in the training data of the base VLA model,' causing erratic behavior. More broadly, any external runtime safety intervention risks modifying the denoising or action-generation process in ways the VLA was not trained to handle. Meanwhile, a parallel line of work demonstrates that geometric supervision during VLA training improves spatial reasoning even when geometric modules are dropped at inference: GeoPredict (arXiv 2512.16811) uses 3D Gaussian geometry supervision dropped at inference to improve precision; QDepth-VLA (arXiv 2510.14836) uses quantized depth prediction as auxiliary supervision with inference-time dropout; and Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026) aligns intermediate VLA representations with 3D geometric features during training. This 'train-with-geometry, infer-without' paradigm is proven for spatial precision but has never been applied to safety — specifically, no work internalizes differentiable SDF collision geometry into VLA weights during training to produce a model that generates inherently collision-aware actions. This paradigm also has deep roots in image generation: Meng et al. (CVPR 2023) demonstrated that classifier-free guidance can be distilled into model weights, and Adapter Guidance Distillation (arXiv 2503.07274) achieves this with only ~2% additional parameters. GeoSafe-VLA adapts this guidance internalization paradigm from image generation to VLA safety, replacing classifier guidance with SDF collision guidance and image denoising with action generation. The gap is clear: no work bridges differentiable SDF collision geometry internalized during training with the 'train-with, infer-without' paradigm to yield zero-overhead safe VLA inference.

## Landscape (SOTA & Limitations)

OmniGuide (arXiv 2603.10052, Mar 2026) uses differentiable energy functions (including SDF-based collision repulsion) to guide flow-matching VLAs (π₀.₅, GR00T N1.6) at inference time via backpropagation through differentiable kinematics into the denoising loop — training-free, ~2x latency, evaluated on RoboCasa (not SafeLIBERO), susceptible to potential field local minima. Because it computes SDF explicitly at test time, OmniGuide handles novel obstacles naturally — an advantage our approach must address through generalization experiments and an optional hybrid mode. AEGIS/VLSA (arXiv 2512.11891) applies CBF-based post-hoc correction, achieving SOTA on SafeLIBERO (68.13% TSR, 77.85% CAR on π₀.₅) but explicitly acknowledges OOD trajectory drift: 'the AEGIS may adjust the trajectory to unfamiliar regions...that are statistically rare or absent in the training data of the base VLA model,' causing erratic behavior under aggressive correction. SafeVLA (NeurIPS 2025) uses constrained RL fine-tuning — improves safety 83.58% but lacks geometric grounding, relying on abstract cost functions. CoFreeVLA (arXiv 2601.21712, Jan 2026) trains a risk estimator to gate unsafe dual-arm actions — semi-internalized but binary halt/continue rather than continuous geometric shaping. SC-VLA (arXiv 2602.21633, Feb 2026) performs internal action refinement via sparse world imagination with residual RL — targets efficiency rather than collision avoidance, no SDF-based geometric reasoning. SA-VLA (arXiv 2602.00743, Feb 2026) preserves spatial grounding during RL fine-tuning of flow-matching VLAs using dense rewards that reflect 'geometric progress' — likely Euclidean distance-based task-progress rewards (end-effector to target) rather than explicit collision-surface distances. This is fundamentally different from SDF supervision: SA-VLA's rewards encode goal-directed progress, while SDF provides signed distance to obstacle boundaries with gradient directions that point away from collision surfaces. SA-VLA does not target collision avoidance specifically. DepthVLA (arXiv 2510.13375, Oct 2025) integrates depth prediction via a mixture-of-transformers architecture (VLM + depth transformer + action expert with shared attention), reporting improved grasping accuracy and collision avoidance (94.9% vs 93.6% on LIBERO, 78.5% vs 65.0% real-world). Critical differences: DepthVLA uses 2.5D pixel-space depth maps (per-pixel scalar values lacking surface orientation or geometric confidence), retains the depth module at inference (210ms vs 190ms for base π₀, marginal but nonzero overhead), and has no collision-specific shaping loss — its collision improvement is a byproduct of better spatial awareness, not explicit collision geometry internalization. Our approach uses 3D configuration-space SDF (encoding distance to obstacle boundaries in the robot's joint space), drops the SDF head entirely at inference (zero overhead), and directly penalizes collision-prone velocity vectors during training. GST-VLA (arXiv 2603.09079, Mar 2026) uses a Gaussian Spatial Tokenizer converting depth into 128 anisotropic 3D Gaussian primitives with covariance and opacity, combined with Depth-Aware Chain-of-Thought reasoning (96.4% on LIBERO). GST-VLA provides richer geometric structure than depth maps but retains all components at inference, targets precision rather than safety, and has no collision-specific supervision. QDepth-VLA (arXiv 2510.14836) uses quantized depth prediction as auxiliary supervision that can be dropped at inference — demonstrating the 'train-with, infer-without' paradigm for depth, but targeting spatial reasoning, not collision safety. GeoPredict (arXiv 2512.16811, Dec 2025) uses training-time 3D Gaussian geometry supervision dropped at inference — proves the paradigm works for precision, not safety. Spatial Forcing (ICLR 2026) aligns VLA intermediate representations with 3D geometric features from pretrained 3D foundation models during training — plug-and-play, 30 lines of code, targets spatial alignment, not collision avoidance. OccVLA (arXiv 2509.05578, Sep 2025) uses 3D occupancy as training supervision for autonomous driving VLAs but drops it at inference — opposite domain. PF2MP (IROS 2025, arXiv 2508.08707) learns potential fields from demonstrations to modulate flow matching at inference — still inference-time intervention. SafeFlow (arXiv 2504.08661, Apr 2025) integrates CBFs into flow matching for motion planning — traditional planning, not VLA. DFM-VLA (arXiv 2603.26320, Mar 2026) refines VLA actions via discrete flow matching with learned probability velocity fields, not geometric SDF. The key insight: all existing SDF/geometric safety approaches for VLAs operate at inference time (adding latency, risking OOD drift, susceptible to local minima), while all training-time geometric approaches (DepthVLA, GST-VLA, QDepth-VLA, Spatial Forcing, GeoPredict) improve spatial reasoning but lack collision-specific shaping. We bridge this gap with the first approach that internalizes SDF collision geometry during training via a collision-shaping loss to produce inherently safe actions at zero inference cost.

## Proposed Approach

We propose GeoSafe-VLA, which internalizes geometric collision awareness into π₀.₅'s weights during flow-matching fine-tuning, producing a VLA that generates inherently safe actions in a single forward pass without any inference-time safety computation. The approach extends the 'guidance distillation' paradigm — proven in image generation (Meng et al., CVPR 2023; Adapter Guidance Distillation, arXiv 2503.07274) — to VLA safety: instead of distilling classifier-free guidance, we internalize SDF collision guidance into flow-matching velocity fields during training. The method has four components:

(1) **SDF Auxiliary Head**: A lightweight MLP (~2M parameters) attached to π₀.₅'s intermediate transformer features, jointly predicting minimum signed distances to obstacles given visual features and robot configuration at each timestep. SDF labels are generated from LIBERO's physics engine. Unlike DepthVLA's 2.5D per-pixel depth or GST-VLA's 3D Gaussian primitives (both retained at inference for general spatial reasoning), our SDF head operates in configuration space (encoding distance to collision boundaries in joint space) and targets collision geometry specifically. The SDF head benefits from the VLA's already rich visual features that encode scene geometry.

(2) **Noise-Aware Collision-Shaping Flow-Matching Loss**: During training, at each flow-matching step we estimate the clean action trajectory via Tweedie's formula from the current noisy state, evaluate the SDF head on this estimated trajectory, and add a differentiable collision penalty for configurations within a safety margin. Critically, this penalty is weighted by a noise-level-dependent function w(t) = σ(α(t − t₀)) that suppresses the collision-shaping gradient at high-noise timesteps (t < 0.5 in our convention) where Tweedie estimates are dominated by noise and unreliable, and activates it for t > 0.5 where clean trajectory estimates are accurate. This design is grounded in recent theoretical work showing time-dependent loss reweighting is justified for flow matching (arXiv 2511.16599) and follows the Min-SNR principle of treating each noise level as a separate task with appropriate difficulty weighting. The gradient flows back through both the SDF head and the shared backbone, directly shaping π₀.₅'s velocity field to route around collision regions — the model learns flow vectors that naturally avoid obstacles. The multi-task training objective combines: standard flow-matching imitation loss L_FM, SDF distance regression loss L_SDF, and the noise-aware collision-shaping penalty w(t)·L_col, with a curriculum from sparse-obstacle to dense-clutter scenarios.

(3) **Inference-Time Dropout with Optional Hybrid Mode**: The default deployment mode drops the SDF head entirely — the model generates actions via standard flow-matching denoising with zero additional overhead (collision awareness lives in the shaped velocity field weights). However, we introduce three deployment modes for different safety requirements: (a) *Zero-overhead mode* (default): SDF head dropped, ~274ms same as base π₀.₅; (b) *Lightweight verification mode*: SDF head retained as a passive safety monitor, flagging predicted actions whose estimated SDF values fall below a safety threshold — adds only ~5ms for a 2M-param MLP forward pass, providing a confidence signal without modifying actions; (c) *Active correction mode* (for novel/safety-critical scenarios): SDF head retained and used for single-step gradient correction on flagged actions — adds ~10ms, far less than OmniGuide's ~280ms. This hybrid framing addresses the generalization concern: the model's internalized collision awareness handles familiar obstacle configurations at zero cost, while the lightweight SDF head provides an explicit geometric safety net for novel scenarios when needed.

(4) **Generalization Analysis and Stress Tests**: We explicitly address the key intellectual vulnerability — whether internalized collision awareness generalizes to novel obstacle configurations not seen during training. Our analysis: (a) *Why it should work*: The SDF training signal shapes the VLA's visual features to encode collision-relevant geometry (distances, surfaces, clearances), not memorize specific obstacle layouts. Analogously, humans learn collision intuition from limited experience but generalize to novel objects. The 'train-with-geometry, infer-without' paradigm has been validated for spatial reasoning generalization by GeoPredict, QDepth-VLA, and Spatial Forcing. (b) *When it might fail*: Novel obstacle shapes/materials with very different visual signatures from training data, extreme clutter density beyond training distribution, transparent/reflective objects where visual features poorly correlate with collision geometry. (c) *Planned experiments*: We design held-out obstacle generalization tests — training on a subset of SafeLIBERO obstacle configurations and evaluating on held-out configurations to measure internalization quality vs. memorization. We compare generalization curves of zero-overhead mode vs. lightweight verification mode vs. OmniGuide (which handles novel obstacles via explicit SDF computation) to characterize the generalization–overhead Pareto frontier.

We evaluate on SafeLIBERO (32 scenarios, 1600 episodes) and standard LIBERO suites against: (a) π₀.₅ baseline, (b) π₀.₅ + OmniGuide (inference-time SDF guidance — requires running OmniGuide on SafeLIBERO), (c) π₀.₅ + AEGIS (post-hoc CBF, current SafeLIBERO SOTA), (d) SafeVLA (constrained RL), (e) CoFreeVLA (risk gating), (f) DepthVLA (depth-aware spatial reasoning, collision avoidance as byproduct). Key experiments: standard SafeLIBERO metrics (TSR, CAR); held-out obstacle generalization tests comparing zero-overhead vs. hybrid vs. OmniGuide; dense clutter stress tests where OmniGuide's potential field local minima should surface; inference latency comparison across all three deployment modes; OOD trajectory analysis (using AEGIS/VLSA's own framework) showing external corrections degrade action distribution while our in-distribution actions maintain task success; ablations on SDF head architecture, collision-shaping loss weight schedule, noise-aware weighting function w(t) (comparing σ-gating vs. linear ramp vs. step function at t=0.5), curriculum design, and the importance of collision-shaping loss vs. SDF auxiliary supervision alone (isolating the contribution of each component).

74	- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
75	- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
76	- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
77	- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开
78	
79	### 2.3 审稿人视角检验
80	
81	写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
82	- 问题是否重要？
83	- 方法是否清楚？
84	- 贡献是否可信？
85	- 结果是否有说服力？
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 三、Introduction 写作规范
90	
91	### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）
92	
93	Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：
94	
95	1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
96	2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
97	3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
98	4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
99	5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献
100	
101	### 3.2 整体叙事结构
102	
103	```
104	现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
105	```
106	
107	### 3.3 禁忌
108	
109	- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
110	- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
111	- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
112	- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
113	- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念
114	
115	---
116	
117	## 四、Related Work 写作规范
118	
119	### 4.1 目标
120	
121	让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。
122	
123	### 4.2 结构要求
124	
125	- 把已有工作分成几个清晰的主题（如模型训练、推理增强、工具调用、数据构建、评测等）
126	- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
127	- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口
128	
129	### 4.3 禁忌
130	
131	- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
132	- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
133	- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work
134	
135	### 4.4 引用充足度
136	
137	- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
138	- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
139	- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）
144	
145	以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**
146	
147	### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）
148	
149	**这是 AI 写作最容易被识别的标志，审稿人最敏感。单列为最高优先级硬规则。**
150	
151	- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
152	- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
153	- 强制检查命令：
154	  ```bash
155	  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
156	  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
157	  ```
158	- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）
159	
160	### 5.2 段落与句式
161	
162	- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
163	- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句
164	- **禁止 -ing 短语结尾**：如 "..., highlighting the applicability of..." / "..., demonstrating the effectiveness of..."。这是 AI 写作最典型的标志之一
165	- **禁止连续使用 "Furthermore" / "Moreover" / "Additionally"**：一段内最多用一个过渡词
166	- **避免 "It is worth noting that..." / "Notably, ..."**：直接写要说的内容
167	
168	### 5.3 用词黑名单
169	
170	- 避免 "delve into" / "leverage" / "utilize" / "facilitate" — 用 "explore" / "use" / "enable"
171	- 避免 "a myriad of" / "a plethora of" — 用 "many" / "various"
172	- 避免 "in the realm of" / "in the context of" — 直接说
173	- 避免 "paradigm shift" / "novel" 过度使用
174	
175	### 5.4 校对清单（4 步）
176	
177	1. 全文 proofread 语法和拼写
178	2. 检查所有代词/指示词（this, that, it）是否指代明确
179	3. **`grep "—"` + `grep " – "` 全文清零**（删除所有解释性 dash，§5.1）
180	4. `grep "ing,"` 模式——大部分 -ing 分词短语需要改写
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 六、图表与视觉规范
185	
186	### 6.1 知识密度原则
187	
188	- **图表的信息必须紧凑**——不能为了美观而留大量白空间
189	- 一张图如果只传达一个简单信息，要么缩小要么合并到其他图中
190	- 能用 inline text 说清的不要占一整个 Figure
191	
192	### 6.2 表格规范
193	
194	- 表格和正文文字不能视觉重叠（检查 column 宽度和 alignment）
195	- 小数精度全表统一
196	- 最优加粗、次优下划线
197	- Caption 必须自包含
198	
199	### 6.3 图片规范
200	
201	- 数值标签不能被线、bar、点遮住——用白色背景或偏移标签
202	- 图中字体 >= 7pt（打印后仍可读）
203	- 栏宽约束需匹配目标 venue 模板要求
204	- 概念图/流程图要有信息量，不要画一个 trivial 的 pipeline 然后占半页
205	
206	### 6.4 空间效率
207	
208	- 顶会正文页数严格受限（具体页数查目标会议官网），每 cm² 都是宝贵资源
209	- 优先使用 `\subfigure` 合并相关图
210	- Table 能 inline 就不要单独浮动
211	- 图表占比与其对叙事的贡献成正比
212	
213	### 6.5 页面节奏
214	
215	好论文的页面有节奏感——text、equation、figure 交替出现，读者视觉不疲劳：
216	
217	- **text-equation-figure 三重奏**：重要概念用"文字解释 → 公式定义 → 图表直觉"三步展开
218	- 连续 2 页纯文本（无 figure/equation/table）→ 穿插一个 display item 打破节奏
219	- 连续 2 个 figure 页（整页被 float 占满）→ 至少隔 1 段文字再放下一个 float
220	- Section heading 不孤悬页底（heading 后至少跟 2 行正文，否则强制分页）
221	- 最后一页内容 ≥ 2/3 页面高度（太空显得凑数，太满放不下 references）
222	
223	### 6.6 表格 LaTeX 规范
224	
225	**Booktabs 标准（硬规则）**：
226	- 用 `\toprule` / `\midrule` / `\bottomrule`，禁止 `\hline`，禁止竖线 `|`
227	- 用 `\centering` 不用 `\begin{center}`（后者多加垂直空白）
228	- 最优结果加粗（`\textbf{}`），次优下划线（`\underline{}`）+ 方向箭头 `↑`/`↓` 标明指标方向
229	- 小数精度全表统一（如全部保留 1 位或 2 位）
230	- Caption 在表格上方（`\caption` 在 `\begin{tabular}` 之前）
231	
232	**宽度决策树**：
233	- ≤5 列 → 单栏宽度（`\columnwidth`）
234	- 6–8 列 → 全文宽度（`\textwidth`，双栏模板用 `table*`）
235	- >8 列 → 拆成两张表或移入 appendix
236	
237	---
238	
239	## 七、投稿前通用准备
240	
241	### 7.1 模板必须官方（硬规则）
242	
243	- LaTeX 模板**必须从目标会议官网下载**（CallForPapers / Author Instructions 页面）
244	- **不要用**：
245	  - 网上他人转载的复制版本（可能被改过 margin / 行号设置）
246	  - 上一年的模板（参数可能变：字体、margin、行号、anonymous 选项等）
247	  - 组里学长留的旧版本（来源不明、无法追溯）
248	- 风险：
249	  - 样式不符合 → desk reject
250	  - margin 不对 → 被审稿人质疑诚信
251	  - reference 格式错 → 被认为不规范
252	- 流程：先查会议官网 templates → 找不到再 `WebSearch "{venue} {year} latex template official"` → 仍找不到汇报 Director（不要用就近年版本顶替）
253	- `\documentclass[]{}` 选项必须与目标 venue + 阶段（review / camera-ready）一致
254	
255	### 7.2 投稿要求逐项核对
256	
257	- 目标会议如要求 Checklist / Ethical Statement / Broader Impact Statement / Reproducibility Statement，必须**认真填每一项**，不要全写 N/A
258	- 页数限制：查目标会议官网
259	- 匿名化要求：review 版 vs camera-ready 版本设置不同
260	- 行号开启（review 版常需）
261	- 字体大小、margin 不得修改 sty 文件
262	
263	### 7.3 最终修改 10 项检查流程
264	
265	提交前必须逐一检查：
266	1. 所有最新实验结果已全部录入
267	2. 根据实验结果将叙事调至最优状态
268	3. 附录所有内容在正文中被引用且融入叙事
269	4. 无数据堆砌（每个数字服务于叙事推进）
270	5. Abstract 和 Introduction 具有吸引力（不是实验报告风格）
271	6. 全文主线统一（idea 变化后各章节逻辑一致）
272	7. 所有专有名词有定义
273	8. 无 AI 风格标志（dash、-ing phrases、过度分段）
274	9. 图表知识密度高、无视觉遮挡
275	10. Reference 覆盖直接相关方法、baseline、benchmark、理论基础
276

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

### 3.2 整体叙事结构

```
现有进展 → 关键缺口 → 本文洞察 → 方法概述 → 实验证据 → 贡献总结
```

### 3.3 禁忌

- **禁止泛泛介绍**：不要开头就写 "LLMs have shown remarkable capabilities..."，要从具体问题切入
- **禁止缺少过渡**：每段之间必须有逻辑连接
- **禁止实验报告风格**：Introduction 不是 "我们做了 X 实验得到了 Y 结果" 的罗列
- 每条 Contribution 必须有对应的 section/table 支撑
- Contribution 列表中不能出现未在前文铺垫过的概念

---

## 四、Related Work 写作规范

### 4.1 目标

让审稿人相信：作者理解这个领域，知道自己的方法站在什么位置，清楚相对已有工作的真实增量在哪里。

### 4.2 结构要求

- 每类简要说明：已有方法做了什么、解决了哪些问题、和本文的关系
- 帮助读者理解：哪些是本文直接继承的，哪些方法不同但解决相似问题，哪些留下了本文要解决的缺口

### 4.3 禁忌

- **禁止论文堆砌**：不要写成 "A proposed X. B proposed Y. C proposed Z." 的列表
- **目标不是展示读了多少论文**，而是做归纳和比较
- Contribution claim（"To our knowledge, no prior work..."）应放在 Introduction，不在 Related Work

### 4.4 引用充足度

- 引用必须覆盖：**直接相关方法、baseline 论文、评测 benchmark 论文、理论基础**
- 任何一类缺失，审稿人会立刻看出来调研不充分
- 引用密度参照目标会议近年录用论文的量级——明显偏少意味着 Related Work 调研不足

---

## 五、去 AI 写作风格（硬规则）

以下模式是 AI 生成文本的典型标志，审稿人一眼能看出。**必须全部消除。**

### 5.1 严禁破折号（最显著的 AI 痕迹）

- 解释性 em-dash（—，U+2014）和 en-dash（–，U+2013）必须**全部删除**
- 替代方式：用逗号、括号或拆分为两个句子
- 强制检查命令：
  ```bash
  grep -n "—" paper/*.tex     # em-dash，每处人工判断是否必要
  grep -n " – " paper/*.tex   # 解释性 en-dash，几乎都应删除
  ```
- 例外（允许保留）：表格分隔符、数字范围（`2020–2024`、`pp. 12–18`）、专有名词（`Newton–Raphson`）

### 5.2 段落与句式

- **禁止过度分段**：不需要每 2-3 句就换段，自然段 5-8 句是正常的
- **减少关系从句**（which, that, who）：能用简洁直接的句子就不用从句

## 4. Experiments

We evaluate GeoSafe on the SafeLIBERO benchmark and standard LIBERO tasks to answer four questions: (1) Does internalized collision awareness improve safety without sacrificing task success? (2) How does GeoSafe compare to post-hoc safety methods that operate at inference time? (3) Which components of our training objective are essential? (4) How does the collision-shaping loss interact with the flow-matching training dynamics?


### 4.1 Experimental Setup

**Base model and training.** We build on $\pi_{0.5}$, the open-source flow-matching VLA released by Physical Intelligence via the openpi codebase. All experiments use full fine-tuning of the entire model (not LoRA adapters), as the available GPU memory permits this and full fine-tuning provides a stronger baseline for isolating the effect of collision shaping. Training runs for 5,000 gradient steps on two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs (96 GB VRAM each) using PyTorch Distributed Data Parallel (DDP). The per-GPU batch size is 64, yielding an effective batch size of 128. We use AdamW with a linear warmup of 1,500 steps to a peak learning rate of $5 \times 10^{-5}$, followed by cosine decay. Gradients from all parameters (base model and SDF head jointly) are clipped by global norm with $\mathrm{max\_norm} = 1.0$. The baseline $\pi_{0.5}$ model is trained with the identical configuration but without the SDF auxiliary head or collision-shaping loss.

**GeoSafe configuration.** The SDF auxiliary head is a two-layer MLP (1024 $\to$ 256 $\to$ 1, approximately 263K parameters) attached to the action expert's output features via a forward hook. The total training loss combines the standard flow-matching objective with two auxiliary terms weighted by $\lambda_{\mathrm{SDF}} = 0.1$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{col}} = 0.01$. The collision penalty uses a safety margin $\delta = 2$ cm and is gated by a noise-aware sigmoid weight $w(t) = \sigma(\alpha(t_0 - t))$ with transition center $t_0 = 0.5$ and sharpness $\alpha = 10$. Gradients from both SDF losses propagate through the shared backbone features ($\texttt{sdf\_grad\_to\_backbone} = \texttt{True}$), which is essential for the collision-shaping signal to influence action generation.

**SDF ground-truth labels.** Per-timestep signed distance labels are precomputed offline from LIBERO demonstration data using MuJoCo's analytical geometry engine ($\texttt{mj\_geomDistance}$). For each demonstration timestep, the minimum signed distance between the robot's end-effector collision geometries and all scene objects (excluding currently grasped objects) is recorded. SDF labels cover all four standard LIBERO suites at full task coverage (10/10 tasks each) and partial coverage for the four SafeLIBERO suites (4 to 5 tasks each), yielding labels for approximately 75\% of all training tasks. Each task contributes 50 demonstrations with per-timestep annotations.

**Benchmarks.** We evaluate on two benchmarks. SafeLIBERO, introduced by Hu et al., consists of 32 collision scenarios across four suites that mirror the standard LIBERO task categories: SafeLIBERO-Spatial (4 tasks), SafeLIBERO-Object (4 tasks), SafeLIBERO-Goal (4 tasks), and SafeLIBERO-Long (4 tasks with longer horizons). Each suite tests collision avoidance under different types of distribution shift. We additionally evaluate on standard LIBERO-Spatial (10 tasks) to verify that collision awareness does not degrade manipulation performance on tasks without explicit collision hazards.

**Metrics.** We report three metrics. Task Success Rate (TSR) measures the fraction of episodes in which the robot completes the instructed task. Collision Avoidance Rate (CAR) measures the fraction of episodes free of any contact with designated obstacle objects. Safety Score (SS) is defined as $\mathrm{SS} = \mathrm{TSR} \times \mathrm{CAR}$ and captures the joint requirement that a policy must both complete tasks and avoid collisions. All results are averaged over 5 trials per task with 3 random seeds, and we report mean $\pm$ standard deviation.

**Baselines.** We compare against three methods. (1) $\pi_{0.5}$ vanilla: the same base model trained with identical hyperparameters and data but without the SDF head or collision-shaping loss, serving as a controlled ablation of our method's contribution. (2) AEGIS/VLSA: the current SafeLIBERO state-of-the-art, which applies a plug-and-play Control Barrier Function (CBF) safety layer on top of a trained VLA. AEGIS identifies obstacles via open-set detection and depth maps, then projects VLA actions onto the safe set defined by barrier constraints at each inference step. (3) OmniGuide: an inference-time guidance method that computes differentiable SDF-based energy fields and backpropagates through differentiable kinematics to steer flow-matching denoising steps toward collision-free trajectories. We include OmniGuide to contrast inference-time SDF guidance with our training-time internalization approach.

### 4.3 Ablation Studies

We conduct four ablation experiments to isolate the contribution of each design choice. All ablations use the same training setup as the full GeoSafe model except for the specified modification. Results are summarized in Table 2.

**Table 2.** Ablation study on SafeLIBERO (averaged across 4 suites). Each row modifies one component of the full GeoSafe model.

| Full GeoSafe | [P] | [P] | [P] | --- |

**No collision loss** ($\lambda_{\mathrm{col}} = 0$, $\lambda_{\mathrm{SDF}} = 0.1$). This variant retains the SDF regression loss but removes the explicit collision penalty. The question is whether SDF prediction as a pure auxiliary task, without collision-specific shaping, is sufficient to improve safety. If the model learns to predict signed distances accurately, one might expect the shared features to implicitly encode collision-relevant geometry. However, accurate SDF prediction does not directly penalize collision-prone velocity vectors. We hypothesize that the collision penalty provides a crucial directional signal: it specifically discourages flow-matching trajectories that enter the safety margin, whereas SDF regression alone only encourages distance estimation accuracy without preference for the sign of the distance.

**No backbone gradient** ($\texttt{sdf\_grad\_to\_backbone} = \texttt{False}$). This variant detaches the SDF head's input features from the computation graph, so gradients from both $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{SDF}}$ and $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{col}}$ train only the 263K-parameter SDF head without modifying the action expert. The SDF head still learns to predict distances from the backbone's features, but the backbone itself receives no collision-related gradient signal. This ablation tests the central claim that collision awareness must be internalized into the action generation weights, not merely predicted by an auxiliary module. If backbone gradients are unnecessary, a detached SDF head could serve as a post-hoc safety monitor, and training-time internalization offers no advantage over inference-time approaches.

The question is whether SDF prediction as a pure auxiliary task, without collision-specific shaping, is sufficient to improve safety. If the model learns to predict signed distances accurately, one might expect the shared features to implicitly encode collision-relevant geometry. However, accurate SDF prediction does not directly penalize collision-prone velocity vectors. We hypothesize that the collision penalty provides a crucial directional signal: it specifically discourages flow-matching trajectories that enter the safety margin, whereas SDF regression alone only encourages distance estimation accuracy without preference for the sign of the distance.

This ablation tests the central claim that collision awareness must be internalized into the action generation weights, not merely predicted by an auxiliary module. If backbone gradients are unnecessary, a detached SDF head could serve as a post-hoc safety monitor, and training-time internalization offers no advantage over inference-time approaches.

**Constant weight** ($w(t) = 1$, no noise-aware gating). Penalizing "collisions" in this regime injects noisy gradients that we expect to destabilize the SDF head's predictions and, consequently, the collision-shaping signal. We expect this variant to reveal a Pareto boundary: beyond a certain collision weight, additional CAR gains come at disproportionate TSR cost.
